findings.current: “You’ve been learning martial arts wrong all this time. Who told you to close your eyes?”
findings.defect: The Korean opens with a blunt, familiar insult (이 새끼 이거), which is part of the teasing tone. The English drops it.
findings.rationale: The source uses casual profanity here, consistent with the narrator’s familiar banter with Hyuk Mujin.
findings.replacement: “You little shit, you’ve been learning martial arts wrong all this time. Who told you to close your eyes?”

findings.current: I was afraid my younger sibling would take all my parents’ love
findings.defect: “All” adds a quantity the Korean does not specify.
findings.rationale: The Korean says he feared his younger sibling would take his parents’ love, without saying it was all of it.
findings.replacement: I was afraid my younger sibling would take my parents’ love

findings.current: That even you and Great Hero Jeok would have to risk your lives.
findings.defect: The conjunction makes it sound as though both must risk their lives together. The Korean uses “or” in naming Taekyung and Great Hero Jeok.
findings.rationale: The source says “even you or Great Hero Jeok,” rather than coordinating them with “and.”
findings.replacement: That even you or Great Hero Jeok would have to risk your lives.

findings.current: “Then shut up. I’m keeping you fit to fight.”
findings.defect: “Keeping you fit to fight” suggests maintaining fitness. The source says he is conserving Hyuk Mujin’s fighting strength.
findings.rationale: 전력 보존 means conserving combat strength here, as reinforced by the imminent fight.
findings.replacement: “Then shut up. I’m saving your strength.”

summary: The assembled chapter is largely faithful, with a few small shifts in register, quantity, and meaning.
